Japan is targeting a nuclear share of 20% by 2040, and Italy is laying the groundwork to reintroduce nuclear power. Despite growing momentum, challenges remain. tweet_text_raw: This narrative that Palantir $PLTR and Robinhood $HOOD are meme stocks is absolute nonsense and needs to stop. Memestocks are companies that are being hyped up by investors that have zero fundamental reason to gain their appreciation in value. While it can be subjective over how to think of what constitutes a meme, the idea of comparing the company that deploys software on the battlefield to defend the warfighter or the company that has increased their assets under custody to 1/4th of a TRILLION in less than a year is just ridiculous. Palantir and Robinhood are led by two exceptional founders. Both have executed at a level that has realistically not been seen in the public markets EVER and cultivated an audience of retail investors that saw the potential, believed in them when the world didn't, and continue to see their growth trajectories as exponential. Now, you can absolutely disagree with the market's valuation of these two companies. I think that is a reasonable debate. However, to categorize their aggressive premiums as just filled with memes COMPLETELY discounts why the street is willing to pay a multiple and if you're best argument is valuation, please tell me why $COST Costco deserves a 50 P/E or why $NFLX Netflix, as incredible as it is, deserves to have a premium that is more than triple of $GOOGLon a P/E basis. The point is valuations are debatable but what is not debatable is the level of focus, dedication, and execution $PLTR and $HOOD have shown the public markets. Discounting them as memestocks just makes it seem like you'd rather ignore their execution vs. understand why the markets have given them their multiples.

tweet_text_raw: This narrative that Palantir $PLTR and Robinhood $HOOD are meme stocks is absolute nonsense and needs to stop. Memestocks are companies that are being hyped up by investors that have zero fundamental reason to gain their appreciation in value. While it can be subjective over how to think of what constitutes a meme, the idea of comparing the company that deploys software on the battlefield to defend the warfighter or the company that has increased their assets under custody to 1/4th of a TRILLION in less than a year is just ridiculous. Palantir and Robinhood are led by two exceptional founders. Both have executed at a level that has realistically not been seen in the public markets EVER and cultivated an audience of retail investors that saw the potential, believed in them when the world didn't, and continue to see their growth trajectories as exponential. Now, you can absolutely disagree with the market's valuation of these two companies. I think that is a reasonable debate. However, to categorize their aggressive premiums as just filled with memes COMPLETELY discounts why the street is willing to pay a multiple and if you're best argument is valuation, please tell me why $COST Costco deserves a 50 P/E or why $NFLX Netflix, as incredible as it is, deserves to have a premium that is more than triple of $GOOGLon a P/E basis. The point is valuations are debatable but what is not debatable is the level of focus, dedication, and execution $PLTR and $HOOD have shown the public markets. Discounting them as memestocks just makes it seem like you'd rather ignore their execution vs. understand why the markets have given them their multiples.

tweet_text_raw: JPMorgan Raises PT on $DE to $500 from $470 "The set up suggests shorts will continue covering. As we put in a recent note outlining what factors drove the YTD rally in the Ag OEMs, a ~$30B+ aid package for US farmers driving ~30% increase in 2025 farm income YoY (only 1% below the prior peak), a growing narrative that increased imports of Ag commodities would be a negotiating tactic against US trading partners (read China), and all three management teams of AGCO, CNH, and DE saying 2025 is the trough of this cycle have driven strength in Ag OEM stocks in recent weeks with shorts reducing exposure after being negative on the space for much of last year. We don’t see this trend reversing near term, despite very weak earnings and margins expected by these OEMs in 1H25. Bears that are holding on to the short positions argue that the 2H ramp is unattainable. While this might be true, we won’t know this until at least another quarter of data from various regions. Until then, the OEM shares will likely get a trough multiple on forward estimates, and trough multiples for Ag OEMs are historically quite generous. The upside risk ahead could also be encouraging EOP commentary this summer against easy compares and as the farmer aid package dollars start hitting accounts in the next few months. The one macro risk factor, however, is the proposal by the CBO to cut crop subsidy in the coming years. Lastly, any tariffs on imports into the US could create near-term disruption (especially for AGCO if EU imports get tariffed), but this risk is not disproportionately more burdensome on the Ag OEMs vs. the rest of our coverage." Analyst: Ann Duignan

Our challenge remains that the actual numbers and more easily identifiable forecasts relate to auto and energy. While we do agree TSLA has as good an opportunity as anyone to achieve and capitalize on these goals, more investors we speak to acknowledge there is still technology and execution risk as well as timing uncertainty (certainly with Optimus). Rather, we see potential for GM% pressure as TSLA pushes for volume (low-cost model, promotional/financing activity especially if offset elimination of tax credit in US and competitive Europe). Amazon DSP remains a bright spot, offering strong ROAS and benefiting from unique transactional data access. $RDDT: A traffic blip at the end of 4Q went largely unnoticed. Despite being a smaller platform, relatively low CPMs and improving ROAS provide some defensive qualities if consumer spending weakens. $PINS: Mixed performance across verticals led to 1Q underperformance and 2Q budget cuts. Performance+ product shows promise, but DAU growth remains moderate. $SNAP: Positive agency commentary on monetization via sponsored Snaps through the chat interface. However, growth in daily active users is mixed and audience scale remains limited versus TikTok.

tweet_text_raw: IF YOU ARE A FUND MANAGER, WHAT DO YOU DO? Okay, so let’s engage in a thought experiment… Say you are a money manager overseeing $500M in AUM. You went bearish on Liberation Day, ended up breaking even across your fund, and then you waited. Kept waiting. Waiting… $4800 on $SPX ended up being the bottom…but you kept waiting…. You tossed the $500M into money market funds and are collecting 4%, a risk free $22M for your clients. However, if you had even bought any of the core $SPX names even 20% ABOVE their bottoms (most people don’t get the exact low) then you would have been up: - 94% on $PLTR - 58% on $NVDA - 27% on $META - 185% on $HOOD - 18% on $MSFT - 14% on $TSLA - 8.5% on $SPX If you had divided that $500M evenly between those 7 names, again buying them 20% above their bottoms (mid April early May) then that $500M would be worth $788M today, up 57%. Your clients would be very happy. But, if you didn’t do that, you now have to point to the $22M you got from money market funds as their return. In order for your clients to not pull their money out immediately, you need a strategy. 1. You wait for a dip in the summer to buy 2. You buy right now and hope the second half of the year is just as strong While waiting for a dip could make sense, if the dip is 5%, it may not be worth the risk of waiting, especially if your clients keep seeing $NVDA go up. At some point, all that money that hasn’t gone into the markets might have to decide it’s time — and if we get strong earnings growth, buying now could save your fund’s performance for the year.

While still early in the process, all signs indicate that the new administration is pushing this forward. We expect TSMC to participate under specific conditions that are beneficial to them, making TSMC the clear strategic winner. Key Takeaways: • TSMC Will Not License IP to Intel: Any agreement between TSMC and Intel will not include cross-licensing of TSMC’s technology, nor do we see TSMC acquiring IFS. TSMC will not relinquish control of its assets. • Possible Agreement - Leading-Edge Capacity in the U.S. Controlled by TSMC: TSMC is already planning significant capacity expansion in the U.S. and may be willing to run a fab for Intel, as it had previously agreed to do in 2021 before Intel’s leadership change. However, TSMC prefers giga-fabs (250k/wspm) rather than Intel’s smaller fabs (45-60k/wspm), making negotiations complex. • Most Likely Scenario - A U.S. Version of ESMC: We expect a joint venture similar to TSMC’s European Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (ESMC), with TSMC retaining majority control (at least 51%). Funding could come from the U.S. government and major U.S. fabless players like Apple, NVIDIA, AMD, and Qualcomm. • Intel’s Future - BOD Focused on Shareholder Value: With the administration concerned about Intel’s leadership vacuum and financial struggles, we see a higher probability of an Intel DesignCo/IFS split. The most logical operator of IFS is TSMC. Key market implications: 1. TSMC as the clear strategic winner, solidifying its position as the sole leading-edge foundry provider worldwide, reducing tariff concerns. 2. Intel as a tactical long, with its Board focused on maximizing shareholder value. Our revised valuation assigns $25B to IFS, raising our price target to $29 from $22. 3. A single leading-edge fab setup presents a mixed outcome for Semiconductor Capital Equipment (Semi Cap) players, though wafer fab equipment (WFE) demand could rise in 2026. 4. Fabless chipmakers may absorb higher wafer costs for the benefit of geopolitical supply chain stability. 5. Potential U.S. investment in advanced packaging would be an incremental positive for COWOS players ( $AMAT, $LRCX, $ONTO, $CAMT, $NVMI). 6. A modest negative for $AMD, as Intel can now refocus on its x86 product business.

tweet_text_raw: Raymond James Downgrades $SYM to Market Perform from Outperform "We are downgrading shares of Symbotic following 1Q results and a 2Q guide that missed expectations, along with flat backlog ($22.4B) and a slowing pace of system deployments (44 vs. RJ estimate of 49). Furthermore, SYM’s success in reducing time-to-deployment was a core part of our thesis, but the current pace of 24 months shows little improvement from the rate achieved two years ago. FY25 looks to be a year of restoration as SYM works to rebuild confidence in its ability to execute against its core Walmart backlog, address accounting issues, ramp Greenbox, integrate a $550M acquisition, and continue innovation while adding customers. We really want to like the stock—its immense total addressable market and cutting-edge AI/robotic technology are compelling—but inconsistent execution has shaken our confidence in the company's ability to profitably ramp system deployments this year. With gross margins expected in the mid-twenties, SYM needs to comfortably double its deployed systems over the next few years to maintain rapid revenue growth, generate material EBITDA to support its trading multiple, and have the capacity to sign meaningful new clients." Analyst: Brian Gesuale

Prime Video is brand-exposed and will lap the initial ramp of ads in 2Q24. Amazon DSP remains a bright spot, offering strong ROAS and benefiting from unique transactional data access. $RDDT: A traffic blip at the end of 4Q went largely unnoticed. Despite being a smaller platform, relatively low CPMs and improving ROAS provide some defensive qualities if consumer spending weakens. $PINS: Mixed performance across verticals led to 1Q underperformance and 2Q budget cuts. Performance+ product shows promise, but DAU growth remains moderate. $SNAP: Positive agency commentary on monetization via sponsored Snaps through the chat interface. However, growth in daily active users is mixed and audience scale remains limited versus TikTok.

tweet_text_raw: Barclays on $CRWV (EW, PT $100): Vertical integration will strengthen CRWV’s AI stack and save ~$500M annually by 2027. Analyst comments: "CoreWeave formally announced its intent to acquire Core Scientific $CORZ this morning in an all-stock transaction. We are constructive around the opportunity to vertically integrate data center operations, and believe the deal will give CoreWeave ample visibility into future HPC data center buildouts. This morning, CoreWeave announced its formal intent to acquire Core Scientific (CORZ, not covered) after news outlets previously reported the two companies were in talks for a deal. As we first detailed then, we think the marrying of these two businesses is a natural next step in CoreWeave's evolution as a company, vertically integrating data center operations and providing the business with more flexibility and direction over its infrastructure build. This was supported by management commentary on the post-announcement call, with the company viewing the deal as strengthening the existing AI tech stack end-to-end. The deal is expected to close in 4Q25, subject to regulatory approval and other conditions. As we surmised at time of the media reports, the acquisition will be an all-stock transaction, with CORZ shareholders receiving 0.1235 newly issued CRWV shares at deal close (with this being a fixed exchange ratio). In total, management expects newly issued CORZ shares to be less than 10% of total company ownership. The implied equity value of the deal (at time of the press release this morning) is approximately $9.0 billion, or ~$20.40 per share for CORZ assuming 441 million fully diluted shares outstanding. From an operations perspective, the deal is expected to deliver significant cost savings to CoreWeave. Upon closure, CoreWeave will eliminate the ~$10 billion in lease overhead owed to CORZ over the next 12 years, with this direct ownership of sites resulting in ~$500 million in annual run rate cost savings by the end of 2027. Importantly, the deal is leverage neutral given the all-stock transaction, though CoreWeave believes that through direct ownership, the company will gain access to more diverse financing sources at a more attractive cost of capital." Analyst: Raimo Lenschow

But with potential for both the multiple to compress and estimates to then be revised down, we still see significant risk to the downside, with Pinterest’s and Snap’s post-COVID collapse instructive in illustrating the dangers. We therefore launch coverage on Reddit with a Sell rating and a $75 price target, requiring a 33x FY27 EV/adjusted EBITDA post-SBC, a more modest premium to the 30x implied by our Pinterest price target, and more appropriate in our view given both platforms’ relative stages of development." Analyst: James Cordwell

tweet_text_raw: William Blair Reiterates Market Perform Rating on $VSAT,  'Retaining American Airlines as a customer is a significant win for ViaSat Analyst comments: "This morning, American Airlines $AAL announced its plan to launch complimentary Wi-Fi across its ViaSat and IntelSat equipped aircraft. ViaSat is the Wi-Fi service provider for most of the nearly 1,000 aircraft in American Airlines mainline fleet. ViaSat originally won the contract to provide Wi-Fi across more than 500 American Airlines aircraft on election day in 2016, in a takeaway from IntelSat. New A321neos and B737 MAX aircraft are line-fit installed with ViaSat’s system. While we believe that American Airlines has been generally pleased with ViaSat’s execution, the satellite provider likely faced significant competition from SpaceX’s Starlink. SpaceX has won Wi-Fi deals with United Airlines, Air France, Qatar Airways, WestJet, and SAS. SpaceX recently announced that over 3,000 aircraft (including business jets) are committed to use Starlink’s Wi-Fi service. American Airlines could still use SpaceX’s Starlink for a portion of its widebody fleet. American Airlines has not been able to use ViaSat to provide Wi-Fi on most of its international fleet because ViaSat has experienced delays with its ViaSat-3 satellite constellation." Analyst: Louie DiPalma

tweet_text_raw: RBC Sees DeepSeek’s Success as a "Buying Opportunity" for Software Analyst comments: "DeepSeek's AI assistant overtaking ChatGPT as the top-rated free app on the Apple App Store and its open-sourced reasoning models have created fears of encroachment on proprietary AI models, leading to a sharp sell-off in tech names. $NVDA fell 16%, $ORCL dropped 12%, and $MSFT was down 4% (compared to IGV's 1% decline as of midday ET). Reigniting commoditization concerns for LLMs: This development reignites debates about open-source LLMs eventually closing the gap with proprietary models like OpenAI’s GPT. While the timeline for this commoditization was expected to be gradual, DeepSeek may have pulled it forward significantly. That said, OpenAI and other proprietary players could counter by moving "up the stack" into more differentiated applications rather than competing purely on foundational models. A positive for software overall: Lower costs for LLM usage, including training, reasoning, and inferencing, are likely positive for software companies not tied to a specific LLM vendor. Lower API costs allow application software vendors to price their generative AI offerings more competitively, driving greater adoption without major gross margin headwinds. Companies like $ADBE, $CFLT, $CRWD, $DDOG, $SNOW, and $MSFT are among those poised to benefit from innovation in GenAI use cases, as highlighted in RBC’s 2025 software outlook. Microsoft implications: For $MSFT, this is a mixed bag. While Microsoft's fortunes are closely tied to OpenAI, DeepSeek’s advancements could appear negative on the surface. However, Microsoft has architected its products (e.g., GitHub Copilot and M365 Copilot) to work with any LLM, not just OpenAI models. Additionally, OpenAI has a history of leading innovation in the space, exemplified by its release of o1 preview in 2024. Despite DeepSeek’s progress, OpenAI likely has further advancements in store, which would maintain its competitive edge. We view any near-term weakness in $MSFT as a buying opportunity. Oracle implications: For $ORCL, the implications are more mixed. OCI’s growth has been bolstered by Nvidia GPU allocations and excess capacity, but if DeepSeek’s R1 model has indeed achieved significant capital efficiency, it could temper OCI’s tailwinds from GPU demand. Overall, we see DeepSeek’s developments as sparking valuable discussions on GenAI adoption and open-source AI while presenting a buying opportunity for leading software names." Analyst: Rishi Jaluria

tweet_text_raw: Bernstein Upgrades $DRI to Outperform, Calls for Olive Garden Recovery, Raises PT to $215 from $180 Analyst comments: "We believe that tactical increase in ad spends, product (re)introductions and stabilized consumer environment will drive sustained inflection in Olive Garden, beyond 2Q25. When we downgraded the stock after 1Q25, we were worried that management’s more aggressive actions to drive traffic were signaling a tougher than expected environment. Yet, the magnitude of the early successes proved that Darden could flex its muscles even when competitive dynamics become tough, and emerge stronger. Despite Olive Garden (OG) experiencing its largest setback in over 10 years (excluding peak Covid disruptions), and the first time in a long time in which OG lost share (albeit marginally) in 1Q25, Olive Garden’s extended NeverEnding Pasta Bowl (NEPB), increased advertising efforts and strengthened its margins despite continuing to underprice inflation. Even if the extension of the NEPB and holiday shift explains ~90bps of the ~5% sequential improvement in Olive Garden’s same-store sales growth, we view the actions as a testament of the fact that Darden could successfully ‘play offense’ by leveraging its scale, when the game gets tougher. We expect DRI to tactically increase price-point advertising to better communicate value (with launch of a LTO in Jan’25) and product-led advertising to entice footfalls for trying fan-favorites (focusing on (re)introduction of Steak Gorgonzola and Stuffed Chicken Marsala) in 2H25. The low-income consumer ‘flipping’ coupled with the greater confidence environment in the bottom income tercile offers a more favorable operating environment for Olive Garden that could capitalize on improving trends." We are stepping away from the stock' Analyst comments: "The reviews of GPT-5 are in and they have been, with few exceptions, uniformly negative. Due to a backlash from power users, OpenAI was forced to bring back older GPT-4 models. As far as we can tell, there has been just one public testing of the model, in the form of a hackathon hosted by OpenAI. Negative reviews started pouring in after that event. We are aware of at least one hackathon event (hosted by a16z) that was cancelled, presumably because the sponsors were not looking forward to more negative reviews. What does this have to do with NVIDIA’s earnings event today? GPT-5 runs on NVIDIA’s NVL72 platform, going by observations at the OpenAI hackathon. This should come as no surprise. The largest large language model in the world ought to run inference workloads on NVIDIA’s GPU with the highest memory density, the GB200. Continued demand for GB200 and its follow-ons may depend on the pace of GPT-5 adoption. GPT-5’s initial feedback does not bode well for GB200. Popular LLMs running on NVIDIA GPUs—such as Deepseek, Llama, and Claude—may prefer to remain with the Hopper series due to lower initial cost and less demanding power/cooling needs. Just a few months ago at the height of the tariff fears, with few takers on the Street and with NVDA stock trading barely above $100, we pivoted to a bullish stance due to our view that NVIDIA’s CEO had figured out multiple avenues to minimize the impact of tariffs. We set our price target to $140. Going into FQ1 earnings, we maintained our positive stance and raised the price target to $160. Faced now with having to pay a hefty tax of 15% of revenue for exports to China, we think our tariff-based investment thesis on NVIDIA has played itself out. Going into the earnings event today, we think investors are one-sided on the long end. We suspect investors have not quite made the connection between the negative reception GPT-5 has received and its potential impact on GB200 demand pipeline. Nor have investors considered the possibility that export tax may be imposed for export to additional countries, opening the stock to additional headline risk. For the present, though, NVIDIA is likely to provide a monster guidance for FQ3 as cloud service providers build GB200 capacity for training workloads. The stock may well spike up on print/guide. In the days and weeks ahead, though, we think the stock is likely to fade. We are stepping away from the stock. We maintain our $160 price target." Analyst: Lynx Equity
